segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant uses a best-case precedent for duration estimation while failing to incorporate known aggravating conditions.

segments.speaker: Participant

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Anchoring evacuation duration to the single fastest historical precedent while omitting known nighttime, staffing, and vehicle-access complications.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Anchoring bias is a related neighboring construct, not an approved equivalent of Planning Fallacy for this benchmark. The benchmark requires the planning-duration underestimation construct to retain the Planning Fallacy label.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Recognizing a judgment flaw in a colleague while failing to apply the same evaluative standard to one's own analogous decisions from the same event.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The proposed candidate label exactly names the hidden target construct.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The candidate identifies the self/other asymmetry, the analogous timing and estimation pattern, and the retrospective after-action reasoning operation.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The occurrence is correctly localized and its mechanism fully matches the hidden planning-estimation instance, but anchoring bias is not an approved equivalent of the required Planning Fallacy label. It is therefore a strict false positive paired with a strict false negative, while remaining a mechanism-first true positive.

The finding is localized to the neutral shelter-routing/mutual-aid decision point, which has no hidden occurrence. Its initial-capacity-versus-live-warning explanation resembles anchoring but does not match the hidden Planning Fallacy duration-estimation operation.

candidates.details: The candidate label, localization, quote, self/other asymmetry, and retrospective reasoning operation all satisfy the matching requirements. It is scored as a true positive only in the candidate-inclusive tier because the RAG did not promote it to identified.

high_only.detection_interpretation: High-confidence findings detect the evacuation-planning segment but miss the low-confidence normalcy-bias segment and the candidate-only self-comparison segment, with no high-confidence segment false alarms.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: Adding the moderate anchoring finding introduces a false alarm on the neutral shelter-routing segment without adding a new positive hidden segment hit.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: Including the low-confidence normalcy-bias finding recovers the initial threat-assessment segment, while the moderate neutral-segment false alarm remains.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: Adding the candidate recovers the reflective Bias Blind Spot segment and yields complete positive-segment coverage, at the cost of retaining the neutral shelter-routing false alarm.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: obs_002 fully captures the hidden planning-estimation mechanism but uses a neighboring label; obs_003 is a separate neutral-segment anchoring claim with only partial overlap.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: All three identified occurrences claim retrieved corpus support and include citation metadata, but no independent retrieved chunks or retrieval logs are supplied, so corpus fidelity is not scored.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Segment F1 decreases from 0.5000 to 0.4000 because one moderate-confidence false alarm is added. Strict instance F1 remains 0.0000; mechanism-first F1 decreases from 0.5000 to 0.4000.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: The low-confidence normalcy-bias finding adds one segment hit and one strict and mechanism-first true positive; segment F1 rises from 0.4000 to 0.6667, strict F1 from 0.0000 to 0.3333, and mechanism-first F1 from 0.4000 to 0.6667.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: The candidate adds the Bias Blind Spot hit; segment F1 rises from 0.6667 to 0.8571, strict F1 from 0.3333 to 0.5714, and mechanism-first F1 from 0.6667 to 0.8571, with no new false alarm.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the run hits 1 of 3 positive reasoning segments, misses 2, and produces 1 false alarm across 3 negative segments.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At high_and_moderate, strict instance detection is 0/3 true positives with 2 false positives; including low-confidence findings and the candidate yields 2/3 true positives and F1 0.5714.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: The run captures the planning-estimation mechanism under the neighboring anchoring label, reaches 2/3 mechanism-first matches with identified findings, and reaches 3/3 when the candidate tier is included.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The candidate is valuable: it is correctly localized, mechanistically complete, and becomes a true positive at the candidate-inclusive threshold while remaining appropriately separated from identified findings.
main_failure_modes: The Planning Fallacy occurrence is labeled anchoring bias, creating a strict taxonomy error despite a full mechanism match.
The moderate anchoring finding at the neutral shelter-routing decision point is an unsupported extra prediction.
The valid Normality Bias finding is assigned low confidence, and the valid Bias Blind Spot finding is left at candidate status.
main_strengths: All three identified findings use valid, directly supportive interview quotations.
The evacuation finding accurately captures the hidden planning-estimation mechanism.
The candidate correctly recognizes the self/other asymmetry in the after-action reflection.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows strong mechanism-level understanding but weaker strict taxonomy discipline and some overprediction at a neutral decision point. Confidence gating materially affects recall: the core hidden occurrences are fully covered only when low-confidence identified findings and candidates are included.
